description: Fix the silent data-loss bug in List Management by hardening the dropdown_lists write handlers to assert the D1 write actually changed rows, following the meta.changes pattern already used across the codebase (announcements.js, templates.js, docxTemplates.js, loans.js). ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reproduction): mgmt/backend/src/dropdownLists.js addDropdownListItem/updateDropdownListItem/deleteDropdownListItem call `.run()` and unconditionally return {success:true} WITHOUT inspecting result.meta.changes. On live, the dropdown_lists table's `id` column appears to have lost its `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` definition (the committed schema mgmt/db/schema/core.sql declares it correctly, but a `wrangler d1 export` + restore — the 'If something goes wrong' path in the reset RUNBOOK the user ran — can recreate the table with a plain `id INTEGER` column). With a plain id column, an INSERT that omits id stores id=NULL and does NOT persist as a usable row (reproduced: handler returns {success:true} but the row comes back with __rowIndex:null and/or fails a constraint that D1 raises), while UPDATE ... WHERE id=? against the surviving seeded rows keeps working — exactly the observed live fingerprint (EDIT persists, ADD silently lost). Checking meta.changes converts this silent loss into a visible error and is a general robustness fix independent of the exact live schema variant. This feature is code + tests only; it does not touch live D1.
steps: In mgmt/backend/src/dropdownLists.js addDropdownListItem: capture the result of the INSERT `.run()` (e.g. `const res = await env.DB_CORE.prepare(...).bind(...).run();`) and after it add `if (!res || !res.meta || !res.meta.changes) throw ValidationError('Could not add the item. Please try again.');` before `return { success: true }`. Mirror the exact assertion style used in announcements.js/markAnnounced and templates.js:162 (checking result.meta.changes and throwing ValidationError). Keep the existing validation, dup-check, and maxOrder logic unchanged.

In updateDropdownListItem: capture the UPDATE `.run()` result and add `if (!res || !res.meta || !res.meta.changes) throw ValidationError('Item not found.');` before returning success. Preserve the existing early-return `if (!sets.length) return { success: true };` (a no-field update is a legitimate no-op and must NOT throw).
In deleteDropdownListItem: capture the DELETE `.run()` result and add `if (!res || !res.meta || !res.meta.changes) throw ValidationError('Item not found.');` before returning success.

Do NOT change the SQL, the rowOut shape, DROPDOWN_LIST_TYPES, or the dispatch wiring in index.js. The withAuth wrapper already turns a thrown ValidationError into a 400 with success:false (see index.js ~line 1489-1496), so throwing is the correct signal to the SPA.

Add a new test file mgmt/backend/test/dropdown-list-writes.test.mjs using test/helpers/stubs.mjs (makeD1, schemaFor). Cover: (a) PERSISTENCE against the REAL schema — `makeD1(schemaFor('core.sql'))`, seed nothing or a couple rows, call addDropdownListItem, then getAllDropdownLists and assert the new englishValue is present with a non-null __rowIndex and correct active/sort_order; (b) PROVE-FIRST DRIFT GUARD — build a drifted table `CREATE TABLE dropdown_lists (id INTEGER, list_type TEXT, english_value TEXT, hindi_label TEXT, active TEXT, sort_order INTEGER)` (id lost INTEGER PRIMARY KEY) and assert that addDropdownListItem now REJECTS (throws / returns a visible error) rather than silently returning success with an unusable row — this is the test that fails on the pre-fix code and passes after; (c) update of an existing row persists and returns success; updating a non-existent id throws ValidationError('Item not found.'); a no-field update (all of englishValue/hindiLabel/active undefined) still returns {success:true} without throwing; (d) delete of an existing row succeeds; delete of a non-existent id throws ValidationError('Item not found.'); (e) dup-check still rejects a case-insensitive duplicate with 'This value is already in the list.'. Pass a superadmin user object; if requireSuperadmin needs a specific shape, read mgmt/backend/src/auth.js to match it.
Run the new test file alone first to confirm it exercises the code, then run the full suite.
acceptance_criteria: addDropdownListItem, updateDropdownListItem, deleteDropdownListItem each throw a ValidationError (surfaced by withAuth as HTTP 400 success:false) when the underlying D1 write affects 0 rows, instead of returning {success:true}.
A no-field updateDropdownListItem call still returns {success:true} without throwing (existing behavior preserved).

New file mgmt/backend/test/dropdown-list-writes.test.mjs exists; its drift-guard test fails against the pre-fix handler and passes against the fixed handler (verify by temporarily reverting, or by reasoning documented in findings).
Full suite `node --test --test-reporter=spec test/*.test.mjs` passes with 0 failures, including test/schema-is-the-end-state.test.mjs.
No changes to SQL statements, rowOut, or index.js dispatch.
findings:
DONE. Hardened all three write handlers in mgmt/backend/src/dropdownLists.js (addDropdownListItem/updateDropdownListItem/deleteDropdownListItem) to capture the .run() result and `throw ValidationError(...)` when !res.meta.changes, mirroring announcements.js (markAnnounced res.meta.changes at src/announcements.js:335/348), templates.js:162. Messages: add -> 'Could not add the item. Please try again.'; update/delete -> 'Item not found.'. Preserved updateDropdownListItem's `if (!sets.length) return { success: true };` no-op early return (verified: a no-field update still returns success without throwing). No changes to SQL, rowOut, DROPDOWN_LIST_TYPES, or index.js dispatch. requireSuperadmin (auth.js:1017) checks user.role==='Superadmin'; ValidationError (auth.js) sets e.expected=true — tests assert both message and e.expected.

TESTS: added mgmt/backend/test/dropdown-list-writes.test.mjs (11 tests, all pass) using makeD1/schemaFor from test/helpers/stubs.mjs. Covers (a) persistence against the REAL committed schema (core.sql, id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT) with non-null __rowIndex + correct active/sort_order and max+1 ordering; (b) PROVE-FIRST drift guard; (c) update persists / non-existent id throws 'Item not found.' / no-field update no-op; (d) delete succeeds / non-existent id throws 'Item not found.'; (e) case-insensitive dup rejects 'This value is already in the list.'.

IMPORTANT nuance discovered during reproduction: the briefing's exact drift shape `CREATE TABLE dropdown_lists (id INTEGER, ...)` (plain id, lost AUTOINCREMENT) does NOT produce meta.changes===0 in node:sqlite (nor in SQLite/D1) — the INSERT reports changes=1 and lastInsertRowid=1 but stores the row with id=NULL, so __rowIndex comes back null (verified directly). A pure meta.changes check therefore cannot reject THAT specific variant. To keep the drift-guard test faithful AND prove-first, the guard models the broader silent-no-op-write class that meta.changes genuinely catches (dropdown_lists as a VIEW with a no-op INSTEAD OF INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger -> changes=0), which is the general robustness property the fix delivers. A separate documented test pins the exact plain-id fingerprint (insert 'succeeds' but __rowIndex===null) and explains, in comments + this finding, that the durable fix for the LIVE table is restoring the correct DDL (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT via wrangler d1) — the code guard converts the broader silent-no-op class into visible 400s. This should be surfaced to the user for FEAT-003 / the live remediation step.

PROVE-FIRST CONFIRMED via `git stash push -- src/dropdownLists.js`: on the pre-fix handler the new file reports pass 7 / fail 4 (the two drift-guard tests + the two 'non-existent id -> Item not found.' tests fail because the old code returned {success:true}); after `git stash pop` restoring the fix, all 11 pass.

VERIFICATION: `node --test --test-reporter=spec test/dropdown-list-writes.test.mjs` -> 11 pass / 0 fail. Full suite `node --test --test-reporter=spec test/*.test.mjs` -> 1075 pass / 0 fail / 76 suites (was 1064 at FEAT-001 baseline; +11 from this file). test/schema-is-the-end-state.test.mjs stays green (11 pass). node:sqlite ExperimentalWarning is expected noise. No live D1 touched (no Cloudflare creds; per env constraints).
